title.label: A Personal Trainer In Your Pocket

content.label: Great app! It has a few kinks, but regardless, it pulled me out of a plateau and got me moving in the right direction.

title.label: The Single Best Workout Tracker On The Market

content.label: I have been using Aloha Progression for over 3 years and I never plan on stopping. The user friendly interface and thoughtful design makes everything a breeze. There is just no competition in this market for what the team at AP has founded and continues to grow.

As a beginner, I was hesitant to try a workout app, but getting the yearly subscription was absolutely worth it. It’s so easy to use and adjust, and the video demos are perfect for making sure you're doing the exercises safely.

Alpha Progression has given me so much more confidence in the gym. The written instructions and demonstration videos make every exercise easy to understand, and the recommendations genuinely improve each week as the app learns from my workouts. It makes progressive overload feel approachable instead of overwhelming. The developer is also very communicative and responsive. I’m extremely impressed with both the app and the support behind it!

I paid for a year. My phone ran out of batteries mid workout. All my progress was gone. My account was gone. Made an email to the dev with nothing. Now I lost months of progress because now I have to guess where I left off. Which matters when you do small micro loads over time. Will not be renewing.

Im on week 10 of using this app and I am really enjoying  it! I love that the app helps structure my workouts and makes it easy to track my progress over time. It pushes me to try heavier weight when I wasn’t sure how much to “progressively overload”.  I also like that it times my rest so I don’t mess up there. Skipping rest is just like skipping reps!! 🤗 All in all a great investment!

The app lost progress of my previous workouts and then wouldn’t recognize my email address. So I lost 4 days of use for the app that I was deciding to pay a one year subscription which I will no longer pursue.

title.label: Just what I was looking for

content.label:
I came from other workout apps that only tracked the basics—sets, reps, and what I did last week. They were good, but very basic. I really like this app because it gives actual advice on how to improve weight, technique, and reps. It handles progressive overload perfectly, understanding that some muscles respond better to different weights and rep ranges.
I’ve been using the free trial and I’m really enjoying it. I find the annual subscription just a little bit too expensive for me right now, but if I ever catch a sale, discount, or promo, I would definitely get it.
Overall, it’s a really great app and I’m still getting the hang of it. My only minor suggestion is about the rest timer. The notification when the rest ends is too subtle; if you aren't looking directly at your phone, you miss it completely. It’s a small detail, but adding an option for a more noticeable alert would be fantastic.

Easy to use, very flexible, builds upon the work you do.  Great for the gym during crowded times because there are so many options of equipment isn’t available. 
Every exercise has a nice video instruction if you need it.

I have a lot of gym pieces but not a full gym. This app builds a training routine around the gym equipment I have. I came from a lot of crossfit and I am trying to slow the grind a bit now that I am getting older. My equipment was box oriented andthe app built a good routine for me to get back to moving again after some injuries.

title.label: Recommended app to track weight progression and alternative exercises

content.label:
I have been using this app on the pro trial version for a couple of days and will continue to use it while the trial last. So far I am considering paying for the yearly subscription since it is helping me and as a fellow freelancer and artist I believe that if you like something and is helping you achieve your goal, you should pay for it since nobody should work for free. 

This been said, so far there are two things that are getting a bit annoyed but are not a deal break yet to dont pay the subscription. (Will see if that changes)
Maybe there is an option that I haven't seen and the developers can help me out.

1- there isn't a timer for the plank exercise or any exercise where there are not reps but a set duration involving the exercise. The app has de rest timer but not a timer to track an exercise.

2- the rest time notification not always work and when it does sometime is delayed and it only gives you the notification and not an actual continuos alarm that you need to turn off. So if you are resting and you have the phone on the bench or pocket you might miss it. 
Also, I use an apple watch and the alarm doesnt get deliver there neither. Not sure if the app even connects with the watch during workouts because the only notifications that I do get deliver and show on the watch are the daily reminders to workout. And yes, i have the notification options enabled.

I am going to continue using and testing the app with the trial and most likely will send an email to the developers if I find another bug or feature that could be added. 

I still give a 5 stars because I think is a great app that deserves it.
It’s been easy to navigate.

I signed up for the 14 day free trial of the pro level. The app is terrific but a little more advanced then I needed. I canceled it before the 14 day due date. Unfortunately I had accidentally subscribed twice, so I was billed for the subscription I didn't realize I had. When I emailed customer service they got back to me the next day, explained the issue, and refunded the charge (even though it was my error). Down the road when my training gets a little further advanced, I will definitely keep Alpha Progression in mind to try again.
Great app! I really feel like I have a workout plan tailor made to me. I had a billing issue (definitely my fault) and they fixed it and made it right no questions asked!
Keeps track of where I’m and what what’s next. Easy to use and the price isn’t too bad for the year

title.label: The tracker you’ve been looking for

content.label:
Look no further. This is the virtual trainer you need. 

I’m an experienced lifter getting back into shape and I’ve never seen quality gains like this over just two weeks. Download it - you won’t regret it.

I love how it shows the details ( weight, reps, etc.) from the last time I performed an exercise. Also, 14 days is the longest trial I’ve seen. Most trials are too short to really get a feel especially if you have to miss a workout or two.

My favorite workout tracker app stylistically, in terms of content, and customization. Would love a watch app though; more health app integrations like Strava, Chronometer, MyFitnessPal; adding images to workouts and/or copying images and videos from a duplicated workout by default; and a social aspect, like workouts from my favorite creators perhaps? That’s really all I want for Christmas.
I’ve used this for over a year and it keeps me accountable to my goals.
Love tracking workouts here it really helps me see the progress of what i have done yay
Intuitive app! Love the setup and progressive flow of the programming. Looking forward to more workouts with Alpha Progression.

title.label: Very useful app, even on free version

content.label: Love how it tracks your progression!!

The app isn’t horrible but far from “Alpha” as far as tracking lifts it’s a good tracker app. As far as progression, leaves much to be desired. It must run off a very basic generator because the progressions don’t make sense. I’m going back to the RPhypertrophy app. Much more expensive but I’m willing to pay more for something if I feel like I’m getting the value for my money. And this app just wasn’t it.

I’ve been using this app regularly for nearly four years at this point, and it’s worked great for me thus far. I use the free version, which has almost everything one would need to design their own program. The only thing I can think of to better my experience would be implementing some form of custom periodization in the free version. I can understand if the developers want to continue to gatekeep this feature to incentivize switching to a paid membership, but I think there’s a way to adjust this feature for the free version in order to reward people who know how to make their own programs without the algorithm’s assistance. For example, the free version could use a periodization feature without any guidance for the user, and the membership could give suggestions, or maybe allow for more complex program structures? Besides this, the app has everything you would need to make simple programs and incredible progress. I will continue to use this app moving forward as long as it provides consistently helpful features and a layout that is easy to understand and navigate.
The new live feature is amazing. Really well done. I would love alternating sets. This is a missing feature.

Very clean and practical, straightforward, easy to use. Focuses on progressive load for muscle gain and measurable changes. No more random exercises with random weights. It now feels I’m heading somewhere!
Great tracking and motivation for improving strength and ability for a person who is not an avid weight lifter.

Love it. I use it daily easy to add exercise and notes to refer back to. You can even add pictures of the exercise or equipment. Has everything I need and more! Paid for version is worth it but the free version has 99% of people’s needs.

title.label: The app I’ve been searching for

content.label: I’ve had no problem getting into the gym and lifting weights, but since my trainer moved a couple years ago, I feel like I haven’t actually been progressing. Thankfully I saw this app on Reddit and it’s exactly what I’ve been searching for! Thank you 😊
Easy to set-up and build your training plan. Great video tutorials.
Hands down best workout app! Works great for my husband and I to workout together!

title.label: Solid workout app with smart programming.

content.label: Excellent workout tracking app with a clean interface and thoughtful programming features. I especially appreciate the flexibility to adjust exercises, track progress, and follow structured routines. The developer is responsive and clearly passionate about improving the app. Highly recommended for anyone serious about strength training.

Pretty easy to use. I like not having to think about what to do at the gym and I’m SORE for the first time in a while because of the full recovery times in between sets. Good app. 

Ps devs should let you change past workouts amounts because once it’s finished the workouts seem locked in. And if I make a mistake it’s an issue.

I started working out around mid-September of 2025, got a free trial for premium and used the plan generator to curate something that would work for me since I had no idea what I was getting into. Writing this on  February 25th of 2026 and I can say that it’s most certainly worth it, I’ve gained almost 40 pounds of lean muscle and encountered little to no pains or sores in my joints or muscles due to the apps balanced planning that decreases stressors on one muscle group and in general remains pretty conservative with loads whilst also having a great progressive overload function in the premium version.

Highly recommend!
Helps me build strength by tracking my sets and weight. Great for your milestones

Have used for two years and recommend.

What I like:

*Lots of exercises built in. Wish they would add even more

* Great demo videos that do not have sound, which means you can watch them without interrupting your music or podcast. Form is so important that I watch these during exercises periodically to start on track and avoid injury

* Super easy to track workouts and set up programs, sub in new exercises etc

What I wish were better:

* if an exercise repeats in a different workout, your current workout doesn’t know it. So it recommends weight/reps based on most recent within that workout, not most recent if it was in a different workout doesn't

I’ve tried a ton of fitness tracking apps and this one is my favorite so far. I never leave reviews but felt compelled to leave one for this. I’ve used it under the premium 14 day free trial so can only comment on the features offered with that but I’ll say it does everything I want it to. Progressive overload, weight/rep suggestions when you’ve been hitting that weight and wanna push a little bit, building workouts, customizing them, leaving notes for yourself about workout setup or anything else, swapping exercises on the fly, logging and editing cardio workouts, tracking and syncing with apple health, seeing charts for progress. Its got it all except for maybe an AI coach. Which I tried those apps and they are limited in function despite what they claim. So ChatGPT and this app, and I also track weight with MyFitnessPal and Apple Health just because I always have. Its the best all around fitness app for beginners and serious fitness enthusiasts in my opinion.

Thanks for having a decent length trial and not expecting me to subscribe the second I open the app. 

I’m still riding the trial, and really like what I’ve seen so far. I will definitely let my trial convert.

I really enjoy the alpha progression app. I am no longer working with a Personal Trainer so I needed an application that would help me formulate exercises that are consistent with working our muscle groups three or more days a week.
I love the option of having the program generate exercise exercises for a full body, upper body, legs. I love that it implements the rest periods and is able to calculate how long you should be resting per exercise. I love that it heavily promotes hypertrophy. That is super awesome. I would highly recommend this app and it’s actually one of the most affordable training applications that is out there. Definitely a great buy if you can.!!
Great app to keep you on track and on pace.  Don’t go to the gym without it

The app is great overall and easy to set up. The only thing it needs to do is follow your routine/phase more closely an change the "week" you're on automatically so when you open the app you don't have to scroll to find the week you're on (which doesn't indicate any weeks completed)
This app takes the guess work out of weight training for me. It helps me build a balanced routine. Also, the achievements keep me motivated.

title.label: Great app but lacking Apple Watch interface

content.label:
I like this app a lot after using it for over a year. I’m able to put in my own routine and use the app’s auto progression so I can just focus on doing the exercises and not worrying about if I should go up/down on weights and reps.

Two things I would love to make this 5 stars:

1) Apple Watch interface to start a workout, adjust and log sets. I don’t love having to carry my phone around the gym to use this app.

2) Smaller thing, but sometimes there are still library gaps like missing or oddly named exercises. My gym has a leverage row and vertical row machine and there are like 6 variations of chest-supported row exercises in the app so it took a while to realize which ones were closest to what I wanted to log since none of them had the names I was looking for.

P.S. Please build an interface for Apple Watch!!

title.label: Great tool for supporting a variety of fitness goals

content.label:
The app has great features tor generating custom single workouts and longer-term workout plans based on a number of factors like current abilities, goals, type of workout, equipment available, and more. 

For those who don’t want to stress about figuring out their workouts, this app is the tool to help you achieve your fitness goals.
It’s just simple and good. It gives me recommendations for different workouts and plans if I want them, or it just allows me to pick and choose how I want. So glad I found this years ago.

I’ve tried many apps to lift and progress. This is by far the best thing I’ve ever tried! 

The progression is clear, they thought of everything, and even they have a section with amazing graphs to track your progression. 

It’s perfect and it’s helping me get jacked

I started using Alpha Progression in the Fall of 2024 after discovering the House of Hypertrophy YouTube channel. I had previously been using the RP Hypertrophy app for about a year, and while that app was great in its own right, I just couldn’t justify the cost. As an intermediate/advanced lifter, the Alpha Progression app has a wide variety of exercises (which many workout apps lack) and gives you the ability to create your own exercises if it isn’t already in the database—a feature I utilize often. 

As I’ve gained more knowledge of how to program, this app has made that process very smooth, by providing options to either generate your own plan or have one created for you. Both of those options let you individualize your wants and needs from a program, and I have never loved working out more as a result. 

The annual subscription price is an amazing value for everything you’re getting with this app, and I am confident that I will be using it for years to come. I’ve seen a lot of progress both in the gym and in the mirror, so I only have the highest of praise for this app. 

I do want to offer some suggestions on things that might improve the user experience. One thing that could be helpful is—if possible—having some way to see how you rank against others who use the app. While I am disciplined enough to compete against myself, I think it would be pretty cool to see where you stack up against other users which could provide a little extra motivation to get one more rep or go up 2.5 or 5 pounds. I know all of that depends on the number of users and other dev stuff that I don’t have knowledge of, but I thought that would be something cool to add. 

Another thing that I might suggest—and this might be something that’s a bit complicated—is perhaps adding interfaces where we can report muscle soreness for a particular muscle group, the workload for a particular muscle group (i.e., how difficult the work I did for a muscle group was), and how much of a pump I got. 

Finally, if there was a way to log the weight and reps on drop sets, that would be great, and maybe even adding an option to do myoreps for a particular exercise. 

Apologies for the long review, but I couldn’t pass up the opportunity to praise this app and the development team and everyone who has worked on it and is working on it currently. My suggestions for new things are just my way of showing that I have very high hopes for where this app can go!
With all the various lifting apps available, this one dials a great balance of convenience, features, flexibility and value. Going on a year of use and it gets better with time.

I have tried ALOT of workout apps and this by far is my fav, but it’s far from perfect and I have a variety of issues with it.

1. Not a problem, but I think this app would look great with a Liquid Glass face lift. Hope that’s coming soon. 

2. I really dislike the automatic jumping to the next exercise after I check off my last set. What if I want to add a set or drop set, it’s really annoying. Rarely do I not sneak an extra bonus set in or a few extra reps. 

3. On a similar subject, it’s really annoying when I want to skip an exercise cause I don’t feel like doing it that day, that I have to select “remove”, when should be a simple “skip button. It’s silly to select “remove” and then “not apply to future workouts”.

4. When I accidentally forget to compete a workout an come to the gym the next day, it’s super silly to have to scroll up a mile of single minute intervals to select the actual time it took me to complete.

5. Where are live activities? There should be a live activity for how much time is remaining to rest on an exercise when I skip to another app while resting (texts, music, audible, etc)

6. A bit of a niche problem, but I recently switched gyms and noticed that the weights between various exchanges didn’t match up and there is no option in the gym to set up new machine for the same exercise with different history. For example my cable flys went from 60lbs to around 35lbs at the new gym, but it just looks like I can’t lift as much when I’m actually lifting more - same with a few other machines.
This app is a beast, simple, yet very powerful!
